abstract: An undifferentiated carcinoma of the pancreas in a 50-year-old man was found to be associated with a very elevated level of serum hCG. Syncytiotrophoblastic tumor cells were seen sporadically in the cancer nest, and they showed diffuse positive staining for hCG by immunohistochemical techniques. Positive staining for hCG was also observed in a few mononucleated cancer cells. The results indicated ectopic production of hCG by pancreatic cancer with a choriocarcinomatous feature and tended to support the hypothesis of the retrodifferentiation theory holding that choriocarcinoma is derived from a pre-existing pancreas cancer through metaplastic proliferation.
abstract_ja: 50歳男性の未分化膵癌に、血清hCGの著明な高値が認められた。癌巣内に合胞体栄養膜様腫瘍細胞が散在して認められ、免疫組織化学染色でhCGがびまん性に陽性を示した。少数の単核癌細胞にもhCG陽性が認められた。これらの結果は、絨毛癌様の特徴を有する膵癌による異所性hCG産生を示しており、絨毛癌は既存の膵癌が化生性増殖を経て生じるとするレトロディファレンシエーション説を支持する結果であった。
